description: Creditworthiness intake under Article 8(1): Prior to conducting an initial risk assessment on a borrowing file, the institution must register the customer's loan request in its system.

Prohibition on concluding a declined request under Article 5(1): Where the creditor formally denies the loan request and is unwilling to proceed to conclude the credit agreement, final active funding approval must not subsequently follow.

Immediate agreement transition under Article 10(1): Once the consumer formally accepts the finalized credit offer drawn up on a durable medium, the very next workflow step must move the case directly into final active agreement status.
Offer issuance sequencing under Article 5(1): As soon as a credit proposal is drafted, the immediately following step must be system registration of the finalized offer record.

Mandatory dispatch of created offer under Article 5(1): Whenever a formalized credit offer record is persisted in the system, pre-contractual terms must subsequently be transmitted to the prospective borrower.

Prohibition on approving a refused offer under Article 8(1): Prior to granting final credit agreement activation on an application, a previously refused loan offer must not precede final funding approval.
Pre-contractual binding safeguard under Article 5(1): In good time before the consumer signs and accepts the financing offer, pre-contractual information must be provided to them.

Offer formulation upon acceptance under Article 5(1): Whenever a credit application completes formal intake acceptance for processing, a tailored financing offer must subsequently be structured for comparison.
Durable-medium contract copy under Article 10(1): Whenever a financing proposal is drafted, all contracting consumers must subsequently receive a copy on paper or another durable medium.
Post-withdrawal non-binding safeguard under Article 14(4): If an applicant withdraws and cancels the credit application, that cancelled dossier cannot remain active alongside final credit release.
Linked offer revocation under Article 15(1): Whenever a consumer withdraws and cancels a credit application, any associated financing proposal must also be revoked.
Adequate explanations under Article 5(6): Clarifying product terms with the applicant after an offer is issued must precede formal back-office validation of the file.

Re-assessment on credit limit increase under Article 8(2): Whenever a loan application is opened to increase the existing total credit amount (ApplicationType == 'Limit raise'), updated creditworthiness intake acceptance must subsequently take place.
Contractual principal specification under Article 10(2)(d): Before an application receives final funding sign-off, a loan offer stating a valid non-zero credit sum (> 0) must have been drafted.
Right of withdrawal window under Article 14(1): A consumer may cancel the credit application only within 14 calendar days after receiving the transmitted offer terms.

Open-end termination notice window under Article 13(1): Standard termination of an issued loan offer by the consumer may occur only up to one month (30 calendar days) after the offer was communicated.

Creditworthiness scoring prerequisite under Article 8(1): Prior to granting final funding sign-off on an application, the lender must have generated a loan proposal recording a positive applicant credit rating (> 0).
Pre-contractual repayment count under Article 5(1): Prior to delivering a loan proposal to the borrower, the lender must create an offer setting out a positive count of repayment installments (> 0).

Consumer-selected offer prerequisite under Article 5(1): Prior to granting final funding sign-off on an application, the lender must have created a loan proposal marked as selected in line with the borrower's expressed preferences (Selected == True).
Creditworthiness intake data under Article 8(1): When opening a credit application, the lender must capture sufficient consumer preference data specifying a positive requested loan size (> 0).
Pre-contractual installment disclosure under Article 5(1)(h): Every credit proposal drafted for consumer comparison must specify a positive periodic monthly installment amount (> 0).
Post-withdrawal settlement deadline under Article 14(3): Whenever the borrower cancels a credit application, the related credit proposal must subsequently be cancelled within 30 calendar days.
Post-acceptance funding SLA under Article 14(1): Whenever a consumer accepts a finalized credit offer, the creditor must transition the loan into active disbursement approval within 14 calendar days.

Minimum financed principal threshold under Article 16(4): Prior to granting final funding approval on any credit agreement, the lender must have drafted a loan offer specifying a principal exceeding EUR 10,000 (OfferedAmount > 10000).

Post-validation outreach window under Article 18(2): Whenever a credit application enters formal back-office validation, staff outreach regarding incomplete borrower files must take place within 30 calendar days (one month).

Post-rejection offer remediation under Article 9(2): Whenever a credit application is formally rejected, the creditor must subsequently generate a revised credit offer with updated terms for the applicant.
Early repayment compensation limit under Article 16(2): Every generated loan proposal must record an early repayment compensation fee not exceeding 1.0% of the repaid amount.

Short-term credit activation window under Article 2(3): Whenever pre-contractual offer terms have been sent out to the borrower, final active credit approval must follow within 90 calendar days (three months).

Adequate explanations duty under Article 5(6): Whenever a credit proposal involving a positive borrowing request (> 0) has been sent out to the consumer, staff follow-up to provide adequate explanations must subsequently take place.
Contractual duration disclosure under Article 10(2): Any credit proposal generated for a borrower must specify a positive repayment schedule duration (> 0 installments).
